questions.question:
The orders team reports that requests to `http://web:80/` from Pods in namespace `drill-variation-a` fail. The platform team says the `web` frontend itself looks healthy. The frontend is serving live traffic for other consumers, so its running Pods must not be restarted or replaced while you fix this. A second workload, the `report` Deployment, shares the namespace and must not be disturbed.

1. Make `http://web:80/` work from inside the namespace.
2. Only `web` Pods must answer on that name, and the load must be spread across all three `web` Pods.
3. You may change anything in the namespace EXCEPT the `web` Deployment: its generation must stay unchanged and the three running `web` Pods must keep running with their current identities - do not restart, delete or replace them. Fix the Service, not the Deployment.

verification.description: Service web selector matches the web Pod labels exactly
Deployment web generation is unchanged and the 3 web Pods were not restarted/replaced
3 ready endpoints behind web and http://web:80/ answers from inside the namespace

questions.question:
After a change last night, requests to `http://web:80/` from Pods in namespace `drill-variation-b` fail. The `web` Pods exist and are not crashing, and a Service named `web` is in place. This team's rule: **an unhealthy `web` Pod must never receive traffic** - whatever you do, that guarantee stays in place. The `report` Deployment shares the namespace; leave it alone.

1. Make `http://web:80/` work from inside the namespace - all three `web` Pods must become Ready and receive traffic.
2. The readiness check must REMAIN defined on the Deployment: you may change what it checks, but you may not remove it. Do not set `publishNotReadyAddresses` on the Service.
3. Hint: use the Pod's logs and a test request to find a path the app actually answers on.

verification.description: Deployment web still defines a readinessProbe and it now checks path / on port 80
Service web does not set publishNotReadyAddresses
All 3 web Pods are Ready and the EndpointSlice lists 3 ready addresses
http://web:80/ answers from inside the namespace

questions.question:
In namespace `logging` create a DaemonSet named `log-shipper` that runs a log-shipping agent on every node of the cluster:

1. Pod template label `app=log-shipper` - the selector must match it.
2. Container named `agent`, image `busybox:1.36`, running `sh -c 'while true; do sleep 3600; done'`.
3. Exactly one `log-shipper` pod must run on every node, including the control-plane node.
4. Wait until all pods are Running.

verification.description: DaemonSet log-shipper exists with matching selector/template labels and the required container
One log-shipper pod runs on every node of the cluster
All log-shipper pods are Running

questions.question:
In namespace `image-security` the Deployment `web` must authenticate to a private registry for future image pulls.

1. Create a Secret named `private-reg-cred` of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` for registry `myprivateregistry.com:5000` with username `dock_user`, password `dock_password` and email `dock_user@myprivateregistry.com`.
2. Configure the Deployment `web` to use this Secret as an `imagePullSecret`.
3. Do NOT change the Deployment's image - it must stay `nginx:1.27` and keep running.

verification.description: Secret private-reg-cred is a dockerconfigjson secret for myprivateregistry.com:5000 with the required credentials
Deployment web uses private-reg-cred as an imagePullSecret
Deployment web still runs image nginx:1.27 and is fully ready

questions.question:
Node `k3d-cluster-agent-1` needs maintenance. In namespace `maintenance` the Deployment `critical-db` (3 replicas) runs the critical database, and a completed Job named `maintenance-marker` placed its pod on that node.

1. Create a PodDisruptionBudget named `critical-db-pdb` for the `critical-db` Pods with `minAvailable: 2`, so maintenance can never take more than one replica down at a time.
2. Cordon `k3d-cluster-agent-1`, then drain it. The drain must succeed despite DaemonSet-managed pods - use the appropriate `kubectl drain` flags.
3. Confirm the `maintenance-marker` pod has been evicted (it is never recreated).
4. Uncordon the node so it is schedulable again.
5. `critical-db` must end up with 3 ready replicas.

verification.description: PodDisruptionBudget critical-db-pdb exists with minAvailable 2 selecting the critical-db pods
Node k3d-cluster-agent-1 is schedulable (not cordoned)
maintenance-marker pods were evicted (none remain)
Deployment critical-db runs 3 ready replicas

questions.question:
In namespace `admin1401` a Secret named `dotfile-secret` already exists. Create a Pod named `secret-1401`:

1. Image `busybox:1.36`, container named `secret-admin`, command `sleep 4800`.
2. Mount the Secret `dotfile-secret` as a **read-only** volume named `secret-volume` at `/etc/secret-volume`.
3. Schedule the pod on node `k3d-cluster-agent-0` (add a nodeSelector).
4. The pod must be Running.

verification.description: Pod secret-1401 mounts secret dotfile-secret as read-only volume secret-volume at /etc/secret-volume
Pod secret-1401 has nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=k3d-cluster-agent-0
Pod secret-1401 is Running with container secret-admin (busybox:1.36) and the mounted secret files exist

questions.question:
Export the deployment inventory of namespace `admin2406` to the file `/tmp/exam/outputs/admin2406_data` on `ckad9999`.

1. Use kubectl **custom-columns** output with exactly these columns, in this order: `DEPLOYMENT` (`.metadata.name`), `CONTAINER_IMAGE` (`.spec.template.spec.containers[].image`), `READY_REPLICAS` (`.status.readyReplicas`), `NAMESPACE` (`.metadata.namespace`).
2. Rows must be sorted by deployment name (ascending).
3. The file must contain the column header row.

verification.description: File exists with the exact header row DEPLOYMENT CONTAINER_IMAGE READY_REPLICAS NAMESPACE
Every row matches the live state of the admin2406 deployments (name, image, ready replicas, namespace)
Rows are sorted by deployment name ascending

questions.question:
The Deployment `alpha-mysql` in namespace `alpha` was deployed with a PersistentVolume already provisioned for it, but its Pods are not running.

1. Inspect the Pod's events and the PersistentVolume `alpha-pv` to find what is missing.
2. Create the PersistentVolumeClaim `mysql-alpha-pvc` so it claims storage from `alpha-pv` - match the PV's capacity, access mode and storage class.
3. Do NOT alter the PersistentVolume `alpha-pv`.
4. Once the claim binds, the Pod must run with the volume mounted at `/var/lib/mysql` (already configured in the Deployment).

verification.description: PVC mysql-alpha-pvc exists with 1Gi ReadWriteOnce on storage class slow
PVC mysql-alpha-pvc is Bound to alpha-pv
Deployment alpha-mysql is Ready, the pod runs, and alpha-pv is unaltered

questions.question:
In namespace `cyan-ns` the nginx app behind Service `cyan-svc` (port `80`) must only be accessible from the Pod `cyan-white`. Right now the app is **not accessible from anywhere**.

1. Fix the NetworkPolicy `cyan-np` so that only Pods labeled `client=white` in this namespace can reach the app on port `80`; `cyan-black` must not be able to reach it.
2. You may edit the policy but you must NOT delete it, and it must keep selecting the `cyan-app` Pods.
3. Verify `cyan-white` can reach `http://cyan-svc:80/`.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy cyan-np still exists, selects app=cyan-app and declares Ingress
Ingress rule allows port 80
Ingress from is constrained to client=white pods (namespaceSelector+podSelector combined, nothing broader)
cyan-white can reach http://cyan-svc:80/

questions.question:
In namespace `init-ex` create a Pod named `init-demo`:

1. Main container named `app`, image `nginx:1.27`.
2. An **init container** named `init-setup`, image `busybox:1.36`, running `sh -c 'echo preparing; sleep 10'` - it must complete before the main container starts.
3. Label the Pod `app=init-demo`.
4. Schedule the Pod on node `k3d-cluster-agent-0` (add a nodeSelector).
5. The Pod must be Running and Ready.

verification.description: Pod init-demo has init container init-setup (busybox:1.36) running 'echo preparing; sleep 10'
Pod init-demo has nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=k3d-cluster-agent-0
Init container completed and the app container (nginx:1.27) is Running with the Pod Ready
